races.name: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed)

runners_data.name: Gomez Addams
runners_data.note: Strong form profile including two recent wins on Good ground makes this a live contender, but De Bromhead's runner is a natural front-grabber who is unlikely to access a prominent position in this congested field — racing further back than ideal could blunt its finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Magico
runners_data.note: Mullins-Townend combination is always significant, and Magico has winning form on Good going, but the five-time starter has been inconsistent — shown P on the map, should get a clean run if others jostle ahead of him, but lacks the track record to inspire full confidence.

runners_data.name: Porcupine Bank
runners_data.note: Top-rated on OR at 130, Elliott's four-year-old has won two of three starts on Good ground and arrives on a 63-day break — Sam Ewing has the skills to sit just off the leader and deliver a challenge, making this a leading candidate if the map plays out simply.

runners_data.name: Brosna Town
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator wearing a tongue-strap, Rabbitt's mount hit the frame over 2m4f on Good ground 23 days ago — will need the pace to be strong enough to close into, which a controlled Fastnet Crystal tempo may not provide.

runners_data.name: Bruise Hill
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, Burke's runner has failed to place in any of four starts on Good ground — Sean Flanagan is working with limited material here and the race shape offers nothing to compensate for that form deficiency.

runners_data.name: Lizzie Twigg
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy partners a mare with three wins from four starts on Good going and excellent course form — drawn to get a clean prominent position just off Fastnet Crystal, this profile is ideally suited to the likely race shape and she is the standout second-string contender.

runners_data.name: Milan Forth
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old ran just four days ago (tongue-strap, fitness not the question) and has placed consistently over 2m4f on Good ground — Kevin Healy will look to track the leaders but this gelding's form suggests placed efforts rather than winning bursts from prominent.

runners_data.name: Fastnet Crystal
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the field, Slevin can dictate a sustainable pace on Good ground without a single rival likely to seriously contest the lead — tongue-strap fitted, won over further on Good going 14 days ago, and O'Brien's T14 rate of 19/64 underlines a yard firing.

runners_data.name: Brave Lady
runners_data.note: Consistent mare with three placed efforts from five runs on Good going, but Fahey's runner is a natural prominent type who cannot access that position in this field — Gilligan will be forced wide or further back than suits, and the 0W record in this company tempers enthusiasm.

races.paceDynamic: Fastnet Crystal is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse wanting to lead, will control the pace from the front without meaningful pressure — J J Slevin can dictate terms and set a tempo entirely of his own choosing on Good ground. Behind him, Magico, Porcupine Bank, Lizzie Twigg, and Milan Forth all want prominent positions, creating a congested chasing pack two to four lengths off the leader that is likely to shuffle and jostle approaching the turn for home and particularly at the second-last. The field holds more prominent-biased runners than the race shape can accommodate — Gomez Addams and Brave Lady are natural front-grabbers but are unlikely to find the position they want, leaving them racing in an unfamiliar midfield role where their style fit is compromised. On this evidence, the race shape strongly favours a confirmed front-runner controlling from the front or, alternatively, a true prominent mover who secures a clean position just off the leader — patient hold-up horses have little to gain from a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fastnet Crystal Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Fastnet Crystal bowls along at a fair but sustainable pace and the chasing pack behind him fails to coordinate a serious challenge before the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: Slevin sets his own fractions unchallenged and the Good ground allows Fastnet Crystal to find a second wind from the last — front-runner tactics against a fractured and congested pursuing pack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Mover Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Lizzie Twigg or Porcupine Bank sits a crisp second or third throughout and delivers a well-timed challenge from two out.
scenarios.body: With traffic risk reducing options for others, a horse traveling smoothly in a genuine prominent position can sidestep interference and arrive with a clean run at the last — both Kennedy and Ewing are capable of executing this from the front of the chasing pack.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Scrambles Race
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched prominent pack causes interference or falls wide approaching the second-last, disrupting multiple fancied runners.
scenarios.body: With four horses competing for two or three positions, a collision of traffic mid-race could stop the favourite's momentum and open the door for a horse who has found clear air — Magico, sitting patiently for Mullins, would be best placed to exploit the gaps.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the final half-mile and a sustained late run becomes viable.
scenarios.body: Brosna Town and Bruise Hill are the only genuine hold-up types, but Bruise Hill carries a fading-finish flag and Brosna Town's history at this trip and going is inconsistent — this scenario needs a pace collapse that Fastnet Crystal's controlled front-running makes unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Fastnet Crystal sets fractions entirely unchallenged — if J J Slevin gets a soft lead and is never pressured, the Galway straight becomes very difficult for hold-up horses to bridge in time.

Prominent congestion between Magico, Porcupine Bank, Lizzie Twigg, and Milan Forth is likely to produce bumping or checking between the third-last and second-last — watch for any of these losing their rhythm at a critical stage.

Gomez Addams and Brave Lady, both natural prominent movers, may attempt to force their way forward early and create a faster-than-expected early pace — if they push up, Fastnet Crystal's control becomes contested and the race shape changes sharply.

Bruise Hill's fade-in-finish flag combined with four non-placing efforts on Good ground makes this runner a potential danger only if it drifts wide and impedes a rival — watch for interference rather than a serious challenge.
Milan Forth ran just four days ago — monitor in the parade ring and early stages for any sign of fatigue or uncharacteristic behaviour that would signal the quick turnaround has taken a toll.

races.name: Latin Quarter Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Arch Empire
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's hold-up operator has run his best races on Good ground (12/15 sim-going sample, 1W6P) and should sit last or second-last; that makes him the only runner genuinely racing in role from the rear, though 14 days since last run is fine for the yard.

runners_data.name: Begger
runners_data.note: William Harvey's lightly raced 6-year-old has only two chase starts on record (both Good, both unplaced), carries an unfinished jumping profile and the ⚠ flag is well-earned; 72 days off adds to the unknown quantity here.

runners_data.name: Bowensonfire
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride on this Elliott-trained 6-year-old who has won twice on Good and once on Yielding at 16f, so the trip and ground suit — he is a naturally prominent racer who may get that berth given Kennedy's ability to place a horse early in a field overloaded with pace.

runners_data.name: Eclipse Chaser
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins partners this Mullins runner who has placed at up to 23f on Good; he wants to race prominently and a top jockey gives him every chance of securing that position in a field where several rivals will be squeezed back.

runners_data.name: Frankie John
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's gelding won over 20f on Good and wants to race up with the pace, but the surfeit of prominent types here means he is likely to end up in a midfield position that does not suit his natural style, blunting his chance.

runners_data.name: Great Attitude
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner; OR 130 tops the field on ratings and his sole win came on Soft at 16f, so this Good 18f test is unexplored territory, but the key tactical fact is that he faces zero genuine pace opposition and can dictate entirely on his own terms.

runners_data.name: Love Me Tender
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden steers this 5-year-old Mullins mare who won twice at 16f on Good and showed good form up to 22f; she is a genuine prominent type who will find herself forced to race in midfield given the race shape, reducing her effectiveness.

runners_data.name: My Great Mate
runners_data.note: Paul Townend takes the plum booking for Mullins and this 7-year-old has form figures of 1-2 at 18f on Good — strong credentials — but 323 days since last run is a significant fitness question mark, and he too will likely be denied his natural front rank position.

runners_data.name: Robbies Rock
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's 5-year-old won at 14f on Good and placed at 17f on Good (2nd), suggesting the step up to 18f is manageable; he maps as a genuine prominent type who could, given Donoghue's course experience, carve out a position close to the pace.

runners_data.name: William Tell
runners_data.note: David Kelly's 7-year-old ran just six days ago (moderate form, 'U' in latest), and while he has placed at 16f on Good, the quick return and headgear flag deserve monitoring; a 7lb claimer in Peter Smithers softens the hand.

runners_data.name: Jolie Jewel
runners_data.note: Brian McMahon's mare has placed in seven of her last 14 starts on sim going but not yet won over fences on Good; she is a prominent runner whose real style is obscured by redistribution into midfield, and Phillip Enright will need things to go his way to recover her natural position.

races.paceDynamic: Great Attitude is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival likely to genuinely press for the lead, Ricky Doyle can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop across the 2m2f trip on Good turf at Galway. This is a beginners' chase field overloaded with prominent-running types — Bowensonfire, Frankie John, Love Me Tender, My Great Mate, Jolie Jewel and Eclipse Chaser all want to race forward, meaning several will be forced to settle for a position they do not naturally seek. Bowensonfire and Eclipse Chaser look most likely to actually secure prominent berths behind Great Attitude, given their profile and jockey quality (Kennedy, Mullins), while the remainder will be shuffled into a midfield they are not built for. A single uncontested front-runner setting a measured pace on Good ground over a staying trip strongly favours horses able to race prominently or close to the pace — tractable types who can travel in the first three and pounce at the final fence, rather than genuine hold-up horses making ground from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Great Attitude Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Great Attitude leads unchallenged and the pace stays honest but controlled, enabling stamina-backed prominent chasers to dominate.
scenarios.body: Great Attitude sets a fair gallop with Bowensonfire and Eclipse Chaser tracking in the first three, producing a test of quality jumping and class that exposes the crowded midfield.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overwhelm Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Eclipse Chaser or Bowensonfire press Great Attitude into a stronger gallop and the race develops into a proper test of jumping stamina.
scenarios.body: A faster tempo from the front breaks Great Attitude's stranglehold and benefits the horse best able to match strides over fences while staying on — Bowensonfire's two wins at this trip become relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Backmarker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Great Attitude sets a crawl and the midfield becomes congested, allowing a genuine hold-up horse to come from off the pace on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Arch Empire, the only true hold-up type in the field, would benefit from a falsely run race that sees prominent horses cancel each other out; the Elliott yard also has strong recent form at this festival.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Chaos, Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses clash jumping an early fence and the race loses its shape entirely, benefiting a fresh or lightly weighted runner finding clear air.
scenarios.body: William Tell (6 days since last run) or Frankie John could take advantage of a scrambled race if rivals' jumping errors create space; these are low-probability beneficiaries of genuine mishap rather than race shape.

watchPoints.text: Great Attitude (Ricky Doyle) — watch at the early fences: if he jumps poorly or is outpaced in the first half-mile, the entire pace map collapses and the race opens dramatically.

The first two fences will be critical for the cluster of prominent runners — Bowensonfire, Eclipse Chaser, Love Me Tender and My Great Mate will all be jostling for the same three or four positions, raising the risk of interference or a jumping error under pressure.
My Great Mate returns from 323 days off; watch the paddock and early-race behaviour — a well-backed Mullins runner carrying that much absence could drift wide or jump flat at the first.
Begger (Ben Harvey) has an unresolved jumping profile from only two starts; watch for a hesitant or novicey jump at fence one which could unsettle the field behind him given his draw in the pack.
William Tell runs on just six days' rest — monitor early to see whether the quick turnaround leaves him flat or whether he travels with his usual prominent intent behind the early leaders.

races.name: COLM QUINN BMW Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Crescent Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Gavin Cromwell; 1W1P from 8 runs on similar going is fair but not explosive, and 52 days off is manageable — needs a strong pace to close from the rear in this big-field scenario.

runners_data.name: Fort Randall
runners_data.note: Strong Good-ground record (2W4P from 10 similar-going runs) for a 7yo who races from off the pace; Mr O McGill (5) claims help, and recent win and places suggest confidence heading here off 30 days.

runners_data.name: Leave In Secret
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner acting as lone pace-setter, but STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) indicates this is not its natural role; holds the race shape in its hands — if it controls the tempo it is dangerous, but its own form reads 467-74 so winning is a big ask.

runners_data.name: Butter Fingers
runners_data.note: 5yo prominent type for Ross O'Sullivan — recent win on Good over 16f is the key piece of form, only 82 days off; 7lb claimer Shane Markey takes the saddle and the step up to 2m2f is a mild stamina query.

runners_data.name: Ned In The Park
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with 1W5P from 13 similar-going attempts and three recent runs at 20f on Good — genuinely at home here; Mr D Doyle (7) claims, and the form string 1-4932 shows recent near-misses.

runners_data.name: Finnians Row
runners_data.note: 10yo for Dermot McLoughlin who has won twice in the last two starts, both on Good over 20f — course-distance profile fits well; tongue-tie and breast-girth applied, and the 4W6P similar-going record marks him as a serious player in any scenario where prominent types feature.

runners_data.name: Truckers Cruising
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner with T14 3/32 who holds up; form reads 1U6-0P suggesting he has gone backwards since his hurdle win, and the heavy-headgear-only (t) flag combined with zero wins on Good is a concern here.

runners_data.name: Kilbrin Rocco
runners_data.note: Prominent 7yo with 2W3P from 9 Good-ground runs; recent second after a win suggests good form and 82 days off is the only mild question — handles Good well and 16f wins suggest the 18f trip at Galway is fine.

runners_data.name: Party President
runners_data.note: 6yo prominent type 12 days fresh; two wins on Soft and Good but the form 9-P266 is modest and the step up from 16-17f to 18f is a query — trainer A D Leahy quiet (0/1 T14).

runners_data.name: Tell Us This
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Good and has placed at 18-19f; 16 days since last run and Andrew McNamara 0/5 in T14 window — prominent runner with a tidy sim-going record (2W3P from 8) who suits a steady-to-fair pace.

runners_data.name: Cahirdown Boy
runners_data.note: 168 days off is a significant freshness flag for this 11yo; 0W2P on Good and a modest recent form string 84U5- means confidence is limited, though tongue-tie is applied again.

runners_data.name: Drop A Threat
runners_data.note: W P Mullins runner (T14 4/19 is active) racing from hold-up position; 0W0P from 6 similar-going runs is a red flag regardless of stable, and the form 74-0P5 offers little encouragement at 2m2f.

runners_data.name: A Snow White Park
runners_data.note: 5yo for Margaret Mullins with Danny Mullins in the saddle — two recent seconds on Good (20f, 22f) show consistency; sim-going record 1W3P from 8 is solid and the trip suits, making this a quiet each-way interest from a prominent draw.

runners_data.name: Herja
runners_data.note: Hold-up 6yo with 1W8P from 12 Good-ground runs — places without winning is a pattern; Harry Sexton (7) claims, and the trip at 16-20f range suits, though converting all those places into a win here in a 23-runner field is the challenge.

runners_data.name: Giant Haystacks
runners_data.note: Won over 20f Good for Ross O'Sullivan on last start and is a natural front-runner; the redistribution note reflects that the field is too congested for all prominent types to find their spot — Giant Haystacks may have to settle for a midfield role despite wanting to race forward, softening its chance.

runners_data.name: Driveonwill
runners_data.note: Another Ross O'Sullivan prominent type (same stable as Giant Haystacks and Butter Fingers); the natural front-running profile is squeezed out by overcrowding — last time out he unseated and prior to that won at 20f Good, so if he settles he retains ability but racing out of role limits the outlook.

runners_data.name: Stoneyford Lady
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead runner (T14 7/40, very active) just 6 days since last run; a natural prominent racer who wants to be close to the pace, but with too many rivals seeking the same ground she is likely displaced to midfield — 1W4P on similar going and the tongue-tie/breast-girth combo is retained.

runners_data.name: That's About Right
runners_data.note: Hold-up 8yo with 2W5P from 13 Good-ground runs — sound profile on the going; form 45P-04 is modest lately and P J Rothwell (T14 2/32) is not firing, though the horse handles the trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Doubt
runners_data.note: Excellent sim-going record 1W7P from 15 identical conditions — rarely runs a bad race on Good ground; natural front-runner who has been mapped to midfield due to field congestion, meaning this genuine racer from the front must settle for a position against its instincts, which limits its chance relative to its raw form.

runners_data.name: Mount Shenshan
runners_data.note: Unknown style flag for this 8yo Thomas Mullins runner; 0W2P from 8 Good-ground runs and form 45-356 offers little, though Phillip Enright is a competent pilot — a moderate each-way hope at best.

runners_data.name: My Cullen
runners_data.note: Only 4 days since last run for this 6yo John Joseph Hanlon runner — very quick reappearance is notable; 0W2P from 7 Good-ground runs and form -F9052 with a fall in the string is a jumping concern in a 23-runner field.

runners_data.name: Stily
runners_data.note: No jockey listed yet; 0W5P from 14 Good-ground runs is the standout stat — this horse places without winning and is a natural prominent type squeezed out by the sheer weight of similar-style rivals in this field, making it hard to see how it claims the decisive position it needs.

runners_data.name: Max Time
runners_data.note: True hold-up type remapped to midfield due to volume of hold-up horses; the ⚠ fades-in-finish flag is critical — 0W0P from 11 Good-ground runs and form 0-PP04 with a fade tendency makes this a horse to oppose rather than follow, regardless of its mapped position.

races.paceDynamic: Leave In Secret is the one confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner field and, carrying just 166lbs on Good ground over 2m2f at Galway, is expected to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without any serious challenger pushing it for the lead. The pace is therefore likely to be honest but not genuinely strong — a single-horse lead at a controlled tempo rather than a war of attrition. Several runners flagged as redistributed — Giant Haystacks, Stoneyford Lady, Driveonwill, Sea Of Doubt and Stily — are true prominent types who cannot all find their natural position in a field this large; of these, Giant Haystacks and Stoneyford Lady, with experience and class on their side, are most likely to actually secure positions in the chasing group just behind the leader. With one horse dictating at a measured clip, the race will not be run at a pace fierce enough to destroy closers, but the lack of genuine pressure also means hold-up horses face a stern test of their ability to make ground from further back — the profile that benefits most is prominent-to-midfield runners with good form on Good ground who can race handily without burning fuel early, travelling within striking distance when the tempo lifts jumping the final fences.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Handy Runners Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Leave In Secret sets a controlled pace and riders tracking it cruise into contention at the third-last.
scenarios.body: Leave In Secret dictates at a fair but unspectacular gallop, allowing prominent types like Finnians Row, Ned In The Park and Butter Fingers to race smoothly within themselves before asserting from two out; the steady early pace means no energy is wasted and horses with strong Good-ground form in the 2m-2m2f range convert that freshness into a winning finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Leave In Secret is allowed a completely uncontested lead and the chasing pack fails to close the gap on the run-in.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to pressurise the front-runner, Leave In Secret builds a rhythm and carries its momentum over each fence unimpeded, proving hard to peg back; despite its STYLE_FIT flag suggesting it is racing out of its natural role, a field this large and competitive could still gift it a clear passage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is faster than anticipated through a scrappy middle section, emptying the field and leaving room for strong finishers.
scenarios.body: A congested early scramble for positions in a 23-runner chase causes more interference than expected and the pace becomes genuinely taxing by the back straight; horses like Fort Randall, Crescent Moon and Herja who settle well off the pace then find the most energy reserves to close powerfully from the home turn.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes early scrimmaging, multiple fallers or interference disrupt the pack and the race is run at a brutal pace.
scenarios.body: With 23 runners over fences at Galway, crowding at early fences creates errors and unseating, stretching the race apart early and producing a staying test that suits the most durable; horses with proven stamina and bold jumping records over Good ground emerge from the carnage, with Ned In The Park's strong Good-going record and Finnians Row's recent course-distance wins giving them resilience.

watchPoints.text: Leave In Secret controls the entire pace dynamic as the sole confirmed front-runner — if it is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at its own rhythm, the race becomes its to lose and tracking horses must show sharp acceleration off the final fence to catch it.

Giant Haystacks, Stoneyford Lady, Driveonwill and Sea Of Doubt are all natural prominent types crammed into a 23-runner field — watch the first fence and early furlongs for crowding incidents and jumping errors as these horses are forced to race out of their preferred positions.

My Cullen runs just 4 days after its last outing and carries a fall in its recent form string — in a congested big-field steeplechase at Galway, a tired or hesitant jumper is a material interference risk to those around it.

Finnians Row has won his last two starts over the same trip on Good ground and is the standout horse whose form profile matches the expected race shape precisely — his jumping sharpness on the second circuit will be the key moment to watch.

COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap

runners_data.name: Norwalk Havoc
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Mrs Harrington and Shane Foley who needs things to go wrong up front; 51 days off, tongue-tie and tp headgear, and only one placing from five attempts on similar going makes the task steep in this big field.

runners_data.name: Jagged Edge
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a sharp record on Good ground — two wins and two places from five similar-going runs — but Jack Kearney's 3lb claim helps offset a stiff enough mark and the 41-day break is not a concern given the trainer's 0/5 in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Ribee
runners_data.note: Has won twice on Heavy/Soft but the five good-ground runs show zero wins and only one placing, which is a real concern on today's surface; tongue-tie fitted, 104 days off, and Gary Carroll cannot be ignored but the going profile is the red flag.

runners_data.name: Dunum
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has been off 318 days — that layoff for Miss Lupini is the dominant question mark; won on Good over 8f and has decent course-type form, but prominent runner stepping way up in field size after a near year-long break.

runners_data.name: Gleneagle Bay
runners_data.note: Won his last start over 7f on Good for Stephen Thorne and slots in here stepping up to 1m½f — that extra furlong is the key query, but he sits handily and the course form is a positive; Donagh O'Connor takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Hardy Warrior
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner for Joseph Patrick O'Brien and Dylan Browne McMonagle; rated 105 and the top weight, he is racing out of his usual lead role on his best form and his uncontested lead is the pivotal tactical fact of the race, but the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence in him winning from the front.

runners_data.name: Lord Massusus
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose recent form figures of 863678 show relentless near-misses rather than wins; 19 days since last run is sharp and Paddy Harnett's 5lb claim is useful, but he needs a proper gallop to get competitive and won't get it here.

runners_data.name: Far From Dandy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with three top-two finishes from five Good-ground runs for Stephen Thorne, and Ben Coen is a strong booking; the 0 last time is a concern but the prior form over 8f on Good gives him a legitimate chance to travel well in behind the leader.

runners_data.name: Loughrea
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this four-year-old who has won two of his last four on Good going and placed in the other two — an outstanding recent record; drops into a big field but prominent style, good going form, and sharp 12-day turnaround all point to him being a serious player.

runners_data.name: Pierre Royal
runners_data.note: Five runs on Good ground for Adrian McGuinness have returned two wins and three placings — a flawless surface record; 30-day break, prominent racing style, and Adam Caffrey rides; the form and going stats make him one of the most compelling profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: Booyea
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a history on Good going — two wins and four places from twelve similar-ground runs; the b headgear suits, and JM Sheridan rides; needs a stronger pace than Hardy Warrior is likely to provide, which limits the late-running opportunity.

runners_data.name: Orandi
runners_data.note: Has recorded decent good-ground form in terms of placings but the recent runs show finishing positions of 8,7,21,15,21 — deeply concerning; a true prominent type who will be shuffled back against his instincts, and the style-fit discount applies given how far out of position he will race.

runners_data.name: Genuine Article
runners_data.note: Mostly a prominent racer who will be competing for space he cannot get in this field; recent form includes a 23rd and a 15th in staying races that look entirely wrong for him, and the 86-day break adds to the concerns — the redistribution to midfield captures the likely outcome accurately.

runners_data.name: Lady Lilac
runners_data.note: Consistent placer who has run into the frame five times in a row without winning; true prominent racer bumped to midfield by the field's density, which works against her instincts; Reese Holohan's 7lb claim helps the weight, but the style compromise and lack of a win are issues.

runners_data.name: Lir Speciale
runners_data.note: Has the best consistent recent form of any redistributed prominent type — placing 5,4,2,13,3 on Good or similar — but Chris Hayes will be fighting for a position he cannot have in a 21-runner field; the style-fit flag is the real dampener on a horse whose raw figures are decent.

runners_data.name: Terre De Vega
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Kinsella who prefers to be delivered late; hg includes hb (hood and blinkers), and the 46-day break is moderate; one win from eight similar-going runs suggests limited scope, and the controlled pace will make it very hard to reel in prominent horses from deep.

runners_data.name: Howyoulikethat
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type whose last competitive form came on Standard ground at different tracks; Nicola Burns' 5lb claim helps, but a 15-day turnaround on Good going where recent wins came on Standard surfaces makes this a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Kai Lung
runners_data.note: Trained by Willie Mullins — always worth noting — but prior form comes entirely over 16-17f, which is a massive drop in trip; Declan McDonogh rides, yet a prominent racer mapped back into midfield competing at a distance nearly half his recent experience makes the form almost irrelevant.

runners_data.name: Merlin The Wizard
runners_data.note: Two recent wins at 10f and 12f on Good going for RP Cody give this horse class-relative claims; a true hold-up type who has been redistributed to midfield, so the note is that he will likely end up there anyway given his style — the extra distance in his recent wins could be a fitness edge.

runners_data.name: Monvoe
runners_data.note: Three wins from five Good-ground starts for Cody and a very competitive form profile for a three-year-old; a natural prominent racer who will struggle to fulfil that role in this field, pushed back from his preferred position, which significantly blunts the form figures.

runners_data.name: Monoceros
runners_data.note: Young three-year-old for Iain Jardine with a decent recent run of 3,P,3,5,9 form; hold-up style on Good going with one win, and the 23-day turnaround is fresh; no jockey listed which may reflect a late booking, and the profile is of a horse needing cover to come late.

races.paceDynamic: Hardy Warrior is the one confirmed front-runner in this 21-runner handicap and, with no serious challenger for the lead, Dylan Browne McMonagle should be able to control the tempo from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over this mile and a half on Good ground at Galway. The pace will be honest rather than fierce — a single leader dictating on a flat course creates a relatively even tempo that keeps the field compressed and makes it hard for true hold-up horses to generate a decisive finishing surge from the rear. This field is stacked with prominent-running types — Lir Speciale, Orandi, Lady Lilac, Kai Lung, Monvoe and others are genuine front-runners or prominent racers who cannot all secure their natural position, meaning several will be shuffled back against their instincts, crowding the midfield and creating a messy shape behind the leader. With one horse likely to get an uncontested lead at a controlled tempo, the race shape strongly favours horses who can travel in the first half-dozen, keep Hardy Warrior in their sights, and produce a sustained run from a prominent pitch — Loughrea, Pierre Royal and Gleneagle Bay are the profile that benefits most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Hardy Warrior leads at a sustainable pace and the prominent trackers travel smoothly within striking range.
scenarios.body: Hardy Warrior dictates an uncontested, even tempo and the race becomes a test of quality rather than stamina, with those tracking in the first six having first run into the straight; horses who can sit just off the pace and produce an extended gallop rather than a sharp sprint are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Steals
scenarios.trigger: If Hardy Warrior's controlled fractions turn into a slow crawl and the field is caught flat-footed as he kicks turning in.
scenarios.body: With 21 runners and a compressed field, a slow pace followed by a sudden injection of speed from Hardy Warrior catches hold-up and deep-midfield horses unable to quicken past the wall of horses ahead; the front-runner or a horse sitting second or third gets first run and is never caught.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge, Late Runners Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine pace pushes higher than expected as crowded prominent types scramble for position early, burning themselves out and leaving the race open for late finishers.
scenarios.body: Jostling among the redistributed prominent types — Lir Speciale, Monvoe, Orandi — creates a stronger gallop than Hardy Warrior intends, and the race develops into a true stamina test that allows hold-up horses to close from the rear with purpose; Norwalk Havoc and Booyea, who genuinely settle and finish, would be well positioned to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Draw Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large field clusters on one side of the track or a ragged start fractures the race into separate groups with different effective paces.
scenarios.body: With 21 runners on a flat course, positional chaos can result in horses on the unfavoured part of the track running an entirely different race; runners who break cleanly and find a clear passage become disproportionately advantaged regardless of ability.

watchPoints.text: Hardy Warrior's early fractions are the single most important factor — if McMonagle is allowed to roll along uncontested and the pace is falsely slow, prominent horses tracking him (Loughrea, Pierre Royal) will be delivered fresh to the straight with a clear advantage over the field.

Monitor the start closely for Lir Speciale, Orandi, Monvoe and Lady Lilac — if two or more of these redistributed prominent types force their way up from the gate, the effective pace increases sharply and the race shape flips toward the closers.

Kai Lung's huge drop in trip from 16-17f to 1m½f is an extreme form-book anomaly — even with Declan McDonogh, a horse whose entire recent career has been at marathon distances is likely to find this race finishing much faster than he is conditioned for.

Loughrea (trainer-jockey combination, 12-day turnaround, three wins in last four on Good going) and Pierre Royal (five for five in the placings on Good ground) represent the most data-consistent profiles for the dominant scenario — watch how well they travel in the first quarter mile as an early race-shape indicator.

races.paceDynamic: Vlhova is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner 7f handicap at Galway and, critically, faces no genuine pressure for the lead — she can bowl along at a controlled, honest gallop without being harassed, setting a sustainable rather than scorching tempo on Good ground. The prominent contingent — Eddie G, Goal Exceeded, Heliogabalus, Great Mover, Zaraahmando, and Send Harry — will cluster just behind, meaning the race is run at a steady-to-fair pace with a well-organised front group rather than a messy scrap for position. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear: Dragon Of Malta, Alfred Tennyson, Shoot To Kill, Red Hugh O'Donnell, Summer Snow, and Banner Beauty are all genuine come-from-behind horses who will be shuffled into midfield and unable to run their true race, with Eddie G and Goal Exceeded — both proven 7f Good-ground performers for the in-form Adrian McGuinness yard — best placed to secure the prime prominent berths. With one uncontested front-runner setting a fair clip and a densely populated prominent group sitting right behind her, this race shape strongly favours horses who can track the pace from a handy position and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — prominent-to-midfield types with proven stamina for 7f on Good ground hold the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent stalkers dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Vlhova sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent group tracks her through a true-run race before asserting from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Vlhova controls tempo without being pressured, allowing Eddie G and Goal Exceeded to sit just off the pace and produce sustained runs from the two-furlong pole; both have won over this course configuration and distance on Good ground for the red-hot McGuinness stable, and this shape is exactly what their form profile demands.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner outstays all
scenarios.trigger: If Vlhova's uncontested lead results in a slow early gallop that allows her to conserve enough energy to repel challengers through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to press Vlhova for the lead, she settles into a rhythm and produces a flat-race staying performance, proving hard to peg back once the field tries to close from 2f out; her Good-ground prominent profile over this trip suits the conditions exactly, though her step back from further distances is a slight concern.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late closers weave through
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group goes hard enough to set up the race for hold-up horses who thread through beaten rivals in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A genuinely run race sees the front group tire inside the final furlong, creating gaps for horses who have managed to find racing room from their deeper positions; however, because most true hold-up types in this field have been redistributed to midfield and will not get their natural settle, this scenario is structurally compromised and requires everything to fall right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners overdo it chasing Vlhova and the race falls apart late, handing an advantage to whoever avoids trouble.
scenarios.body: A bunched, competitive field sees multiple horses checking or meeting interference as the pace-pressers flatten out, with any horse who finds a clean passage through the melee able to steal the spoils; this is the least likely shape given Vlhova's uncontested advantage, but the large 18-runner field always carries a risk of positional carnage.

watchPoints.text: Vlhova's uncontested lead is the single most important positional factor in the race — watch whether any of the prominent group (Eddie G, Goal Exceeded) presses her early or allows her to coast, as that dictates whether the front end has enough in reserve to hold on.

Eddie G and Goal Exceeded are both prominent types for the same in-form McGuinness yard — watch for stable tactics at the start, as one may be ridden to lead and the other to stalk, which could create a 1-2 for the trainer but requires both to get their position in an 18-runner field.

The 18-runner field at 7f on a right-handed Galway track creates significant risk of early crowding and checking, particularly for the genuine hold-up horses (Shoot To Kill, Mehman, It'sneverjustone) who need a clean run from the off — watch draw positions and early traffic.

Zaraahmando ran just 3 days ago and Red Hugh O'Donnell also ran 3 days ago — watch both at the start for any signs of freshness or fatigue, as quick-turnaround horses in large-field handicaps can either bounce or underperform sharply.

Heliogabalus has won twice on Good ground and Shane Foley's booking elevates him — watch whether he travels prominently from the gate or gets outpaced early, as his best form is over 8f and the 7f trip may mean he needs to race more positively than usual to stay in contention.

races.paceDynamic: Java Wood is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner field and, ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle, is expected to slot onto the lead unchallenged and set a sustainable, controlled tempo on Good ground over 1m½f at Galway. With no natural pace rival to force the issue, the early gallop will be honest but not frantic, meaning the race is unlikely to turn into a true test of stamina — the mid-race pace will be moderate and the decisive move will come in the final two furlongs. This shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel just off a lone front-runner and strike before hold-up horses can wind up from the rear — horses like Bay Of Dreams, Queen Aethelflaed, Bucaneer's Spirit and Cala Bonita are ideally placed to exploit that sweet spot. The field contains significantly more prominent and front-running types than the pace map can accommodate — Minaun View, Elusive Duke, and Ballymagreehan are genuine prominent racers but are displaced to midfield in this crowded shape, with Bay Of Dreams, Faoladh, and Queen Aethelflaed most likely to actually secure the positions immediately behind Java Wood.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Java Wood dictates a comfortable tempo and a prominent racer times their challenge perfectly off the steady pace.
scenarios.body: Java Wood sets a relaxed fractions-based gallop and the race stays together until the final quarter-mile, when horses positioned just off the pace have the clearest daylight; with hold-up horses struggling to generate momentum from deep, the prominent stalker wins a fairly straightforward contest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Java Wood's sustainable pace proves too slow for the field and McMonagle steals a march going into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to close the gap through a messy, moderately-run race, Java Wood simply extends the lead it has built and the riders behind find the task too great; a lone front-runner winning a big handicap on Good ground at Galway is not without precedent when the pace is genuinely controlled.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Scramble, Midfield Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If several of the displaced prominent types push forward aggressively in the early stages and create an uneven, pressured tempo.
scenarios.body: Minaun View, Ballymagreehan, or Elusive Duke pressing forward despite the crowded shape would inject more pace than anticipated, stringing the field out and handing the advantage to horses who can sit mid-division and finish strongly; Showyoutheropes and Lady Arwen, both proven on Good and carrying course form, would be the primary beneficiaries of a more genuinely run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely quickens enough through the middle stages to stretch the field and open ground for hold-up horses to motor home.
scenarios.body: Blues Emperor, Grey Leader, or Loingseoir would need a truly fast-run race to pick off tiring rivals late, which is the least likely outcome given a single unchallenged front-runner and the redistribution of several genuine closers into positions that curtail their natural finishing kick; the style-fit discounts on redistributed hold-up types further reduce confidence in this shape delivering.

watchPoints.text: Java Wood's tempo is the race pivot — if McMonagle crawls to the final turn, horses immediately behind like Bay Of Dreams and Faoladh will have a decisive advantage, but any horse racing hold-up will find the run-in too short to close.|

Minaun View, Ballymagreehan, and Elusive Duke are all genuine prominent racers fighting for limited positions — watch the first 2f for crowding and forcing moves that could unsettle the pace or cost these horses ground and energy.|

Rhythm King returns from 274 days off the track and should be treated with caution on fitness grounds — any market support would need to be assessed against the reality of a horse entirely without a recent racecourse blow-out.|
